# ARC

1. Leaves blow over the sand, Berta the sea turtle lies at the water's edge with Opa Hans's letter for the mermaid Mira on her shell, and Hans sits on the bench by the dunes and waits for Mira's answer to his question whether she will sing in the surf this evening.
2. Berta cannot slide into the sea until the rising tide reaches her, so Emma, five, takes the letter from her shell to carry it herself, and Berta lets her.
3. While Mama Sarah and Papa Daniel spread the blanket on the sand, Emma makes a dot of sunlight dance on the sand with her blue sea-glass, found on this beach last autumn, and says no when her brother Noah asks to hold it, and Papa says they must stay inside the reef, that he will call at the orange evening light, and that Emma must call back.
4. Emma and Noah hold Berta's flipper in the surf, get tails, and breathe under water.
5. Noah swims straight across the reef toward the wreck instead of along Berta's long arc around it, and Emma follows him.
6. Noah reaches the wreck first and shouts it, but the only short way to Mira's side is the narrow gap in the hull and Noah's broad tail fin does not fit it, so Emma, who held his hand and asked him to go first, lets go and swims alone into the dark hull, where the holes in the planks let in no light.
7. Oskar the octopus, who lives in the hull, tells Emma his name, snatches the letter from her hand and hides it, and each time Emma asks for it and comes close he hides it deeper.
8. Emma calls for Mira, but her shout does not carry past the wreck, and she searches the dark hull until Papa's call comes faintly over the water, so she calls back that she is coming, and she still has no letter.
9. Then the first orange beam falls through a hole in the planks and shimmers on the wall, Oskar's arms jerk after the moving light, and Emma sees it.
10. Emma remembers the dot on the sand, holds her sea-glass in the beam, and when the dot dances across the wall Oskar chases it with all his arms, lets go of the letter, and Emma takes it.
11. Emma wedges the sea-glass in the hole so the dot keeps dancing for Oskar to keep, and she swims out the far end of the hull into Mira's cove among the red coral.
12. Emma says her name and hands Mira the letter, and Mira reads it, laughs, and swims with her back through the gap on her slim tail to Noah and across the reef to the surf.
13. At the surf, in the last orange light, Mira sings one note, Opa Hans stands up from the bench and waves before he gives up, and Mama Sarah and Papa Daniel wrap Emma and Noah in the blanket.
14. Emma hugs Mira and says thank you, and when the rising tide lifts Berta, Emma runs into the surf and calls after her that she will see her next autumn, while Berta raises one flipper and swims away.
